title: RX 9070 XT + KDE Wayland: 4K 160 Hz fails on DP 1.4, 4K 120 Hz works
body: Post Hi, I originally posted about this in the Newbie Corner, but after doing more troubleshooting I think this may be a more specific AMDGPU / DRM / KDE Wayland modesetting issue, so I am posting it here where it may be more appropriate. I recently changed my GPU to an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT. My main monitor is an ASUS ROG Strix XG27UCG, connected through DisplayPort. The monitor normally operates at 3840×2160 (4K) and supports refresh rates up to 160 Hz. It also has an ASUS feature called Dual Mode. This allows the monitor itself to switch between its native 4K high-refresh mode and a 1920×1080 high-refresh mode intended for competitive gaming. I mention Dual Mode to explain the capabilities/configuration of the monitor. I have not yet tested Dual Mode with the RX 9070 XT, so I am not reporting any Dual Mode problem with AMD. I previously used this monitor with an NVIDIA GPU and experienced an issue when changing Dual Mode, but that was under a completely different GPU/driver stack. I therefore consider that a separate issue and do not want to use it as evidence for the current AMD problem. Current problem with the RX 9070 XT With the current AMD setup: - 3840×2160 @ 60 Hz works - 3840×2160 @ 120 Hz works and is stable - 3840×2160 @ 160 Hz is problematic When I select 160 Hz, the desktop becomes extremely slow/glitchy and the display configuration does not behave correctly. Returning to 120 Hz restores normal operation. During previous attempts to use the problematic configuration, I captured the following errors: amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: [drm] *ERROR* Unsupported screen format RA24 little-endian (0x34324152) kwin_wayland: Atomic modeset commit failed! Invalid argument kwin_wayland: Applying output configuration failed! 0000:03:00.0 is my RX 9070 XT, so the DRM error is associated with the discrete AMD GPU. DisplayPort configuration The ASUS XG27UCG offers a maximum DisplayPort setting of DisplayPort 1.4, and I currently have DP 1.4 selected in the monitor OSD. The cable is a VESA-certified UGREEN DisplayPort 2.1 cable, advertised as UHBR10 / 40 Gbit/s and supporting DSC. It is backward-compatible with DisplayPort 1.4. So the current connection is: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT │ │ DisplayPort ▼ VESA-certified UGREEN DP 2.1 cable │ ▼ ASUS ROG Strix XG27UCG DisplayPort 1.4 mode I understand that the DP 2.1 cable does not make the monitor itself operate at DP 2.1. The connection should simply operate according to the DP 1.4 capability of the monitor. During troubleshooting I discovered that the monitor had previously been configured for DisplayPort 1.2 in its OSD. I changed this to DisplayPort 1.4 and have left it there. The 160 Hz problem, however, remained. Troubleshooting already performed I have already tested: - Changing the monitor from DP 1.2 to DP 1.4 - Disabling VRR/Adaptive Sync - Testing 8-bit color - Testing lower refresh rates - Using 4K 120 Hz as the stable baseline Neither disabling VRR nor using 8-bit color solved the 160 Hz problem. The important reproducible difference at the moment is: 3840×2160 @ 120 Hz → stable 3840×2160 @ 160 Hz → problematic Since 4K160 has substantially higher bandwidth requirements than 4K120 over the monitor's DP 1.4 connection, I am wondering whether the transition to the higher-bandwidth mode involves DSC or another part of the AMDGPU display path that is exposing the problem. I am not assuming DSC is the cause. I am mentioning it only because it may be one of the technical differences between the working 120 Hz configuration and the problematic 160 Hz configuration. The Atomic modeset commit failed! Invalid argument message also makes me wonder whether this could involve the interaction between AMDGPU/DRM and KWin's atomic modesetting. System information OS: Arch Linux Desktop: KDE Plasma Display server: Wayland GPU: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT GPU architecture: gfx1201 GPU PCI address: 0000:03:00.0 Monitor: ASUS ROG Strix XG27UCG Resolution: 3840×2160 Maximum refresh rate: 160 Hz Connection: DisplayPort Monitor DisplayPort setting: DP 1.4 Cable: UGREEN VESA-certified DisplayPort 2.1 UHBR10 / 40 Gbit/s DSC support Backward compatible with DP 1.4 My current known-good configuration is: 3840×2160 @ 120 Hz DisplayPort 1.4 This configuration is stable. For completeness, the monitor also supports the Dual Mode mentioned above, but again, I have not tested Dual Mode with the RX 9070 XT yet. I intend to test that separately rather than mixing the results with the current 4K160 issue. I would appreciate any advice about additional DRM, AMDGPU or KWin debugging information I should collect while reproducing the 160 Hz problem. In particular, I would like to determine whether this is related to AMDGPU, DSC/high-bandwidth DisplayPort operation, KWin atomic modesetting, or another part of the Linux display stack.
